title: Resin jewellery: mix safely, cast clear, finish well

say: Resin jewellery: mix safely, cast clear, finish well.
This is the video for Module 4 of Advanced Beadwork and Jewellery Making.
Jewellery resin starts as a liquid and becomes a hard, clear plastic through a chemical reaction. You can preserve ankara fabric, flowers and prints inside it.

say: Or worse, the maker develops a skin allergy that stops her using resin for good. So accurate mixing and safety habits are the foundation.

say: Uncured resin irritates skin and eyes, and repeated contact can cause an allergy that may become permanent.
So every session, wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses, open the windows and use a fan to blow fumes out of the room.

cards.d: Nitrile gloves, safety glasses, windows open and a fan blowing fumes out of the room.
Wash it off straight away with soap and water. No vinegar, acetone or alcohol on skin.
Rinse with clean running water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical help.

say: If resin touches your skin, wash it off straight away with soap and water. Do not use vinegar, acetone or alcohol, because solvents can carry resin deeper into the skin.

say: If resin gets in your eyes, rinse with clean running water for at least 15 minutes and seek medical help.
Never work near food or with kitchen cups, and keep children and pets away.

say: Step two. Read your label. A ratio of 1:1 by volume is not the same as 2:1 by weight, because Part A and Part B often weigh different amounts.

panel.rule: Never pour liquid resin down a sink or drain.

say: Here is a worked example. Kemi in Akure has a six-cavity teardrop earring mould and an epoxy mixed 1:1 by volume.

panel.heading: Mixing for an earring mould
items: One cavity, measured with water: 3 ml
Six cavities: 6 × 3 = 18 ml
Add 15%, round up: 22 ml
1:1 by volume: 11 ml Part A, 11 ml Part B

say: She fills one cavity with water from a syringe. It takes 3 ml.

say: So 11 ml of Part A and 11 ml of Part B. She dries the mould completely first, because water makes resin cloudy. She fills all six cavities with only a thin film left.

say: Warm the closed bottles in a bowl of warm tap water for a few minutes. Warmer resin is thinner and lets bubbles out.

panel.heading: Getting rid of bubbles
items: Warm the closed bottles in warm water
Stir slowly, do not whip
Pour in a thin stream into one corner
Quick, moving heat passes only
Cover the mould while it cures

say: Stir slowly in a folding motion. Whipping is the common cause of tiny bubbles.

say: Pop surface bubbles with a toothpick, or a quick, moving pass of a heat gun. Never hold heat in one spot. It can scorch the resin or start a fire.

say: Inclusions must be completely dry. Seal ankara on both sides with a decoupage medium first, or it soaks up resin and turns dark and patchy. Use only a little colourant, so the resin still cures.

panel.heading: Inclusions and a glossy finish
right: Thin UV resin dome for shine
Drill 2 to 3 mm from the edge

say: Sand only cured resin, always wet, with a dust mask and glasses. Work through the grits in order, from 400 up to 2000.
A thin coat of UV resin brings back a glass-like dome. Drill slowly, at least 2 to 3 mm from the edge, with glasses and a mask.

panel.heading: Inclusions and a glossy finish
right: Thin UV resin dome for shine

say: To remember. Measure exactly by the label method. Gloves, glasses and fresh air every time. Wash resin off skin with soap and water.
Cure leftovers solid and never pour resin down a drain. And seal inclusions, sand wet, and dome with thin coats.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Measure exactly by the method on the label
Gloves, glasses and fresh air every time
Resin on skin: soap and water, never solvents
Cure leftovers solid; never down a drain
Seal inclusions; sand wet; dome with thin coats
